source.filename: 2022-Detachable Soft Actuators with Tunable Stiffness Based on Wire Jamming.pdf

actuation: Pneumatic actuation (positive air pressure for fiber-reinforced soft bending actuator)
Vacuum pressure (negative air pressure for wire jamming structure)
constitutive_assumptions: When vacuum pressure is off (unjammed state), inter-wire gaps are non-negligible and each wire is assumed to act as an independent beam.
When vacuum pressure is on (jammed state), wires become cohesive due to friction and are analyzed together as a single unified beam.
Cantilever beam deformation follows Euler-Bernoulli beam theory under applied point force Fe.
Velcro strain-limiting layer is assumed to be inextensible.
Internal air channel geometry is ignored in the finite element (FE) simulation of the fiber-reinforced soft actuator.
Silicone rubber exhibits hyper-elastic material behavior (characterized via uniaxial tensile testing).
control_variables: Wire length (pre-cut to 150 mm and trimmed to 140–150 mm)
Envelope material and film thickness (HDPE film, 0.08 mm thickness)
Cross-sectional layout and installation scheme (rectangular arrangement, layout 2)
Loading speed of the force sensor during bending stiffness measurement (kept slow to match elastic reaction force)
Number of repeated experimental trials per test condition (each test repeated five times)
Fabrication mold parameters and Velcro fastener types (ONE-WRAP 29 double-sided fastener, velour 3165 loop fastener)
dependent_variables: Bending stiffness (ratio of applied force to deflection)
Applied reaction force under specified deflection
Torsional stiffness and measured torque under rotation angle
Free bending angle of soft actuators under inflation pressure
Tip contact force / resistance under deflection
Maximum grasping payload mass of the soft robotic gripper
Maximum lifting weight capacity of the detachable soft glove
Slip threshold deflection and transition regimes (pre-slip, transition, post-slip)

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Wire/fiber jamming structures transition between unjammed and jammed states via vacuum-controlled inter-wire friction, markedly increasing bending stiffness while retaining low unjammed torsional impedance for multi-directional dexterity.

Rectangular wire arrangements eliminate circumferential wire sliding and misalignment observed in circular arrangements, while reverse-gradient trimming of free wire ends prevents localized twisting or arching during bending.
Euler-Bernoulli cantilever beam modeling predicts that bending stiffness of the wire jamming structure scales significantly with the number of wire layers in the thickness direction.
Bending stiffness of an 8 mm thick kraft rope wire jamming structure increased by nearly seven times (reaching 0.89 N/mm at 15 mm deflection) when vacuum pressure changed from 0 kPa to -85 kPa.

Compared with layer jamming, wire jamming exhibits lower torsional stiffness across rotation angles (0° to 60°), enabling better multidirectional compliance and twistability for multi-DOF applications.

Integrating double-sided Velcro as a strain-limiting layer and connector provides a reliable, detachable interface enabling rapid assembly and modular replacement of the wire jamming layer on soft actuators.

Assembling the wire jamming layer increases passive stiffness, requiring 145 kPa positive air pressure to achieve a 90° bend compared to 87 kPa for the bare actuator, while vacuum activation substantially increases tip contact stiffness.

A three-actuator soft gripper doubled its maximum grasping payload under -85 kPa vacuum compared to 0 kPa, and an unassisted detachable soft glove lifted a water payload over 10,000 g at 165 kPa positive pressure and -85 kPa vacuum.

experimental_setup: Three-point bending characterization testbed with support platform, peristaltic vacuum pump (KVP8 PLUS-KB-S), precision digital pressure regulator (ITV2090-312BL5), and a slow-moving force sensor.

Torsional stiffness testbed holding one end fixed with an air hose coupler and the opposite end connected to a servo-driven rotating fixture (0° to 60°) while permitting axial sliding, monitored with a torque sensor.
Soft actuator free bending angle setup utilizing a nine-axis tip-mounted gyroscope (JY901S) under variable positive inflation pressures.
Tip contact stiffness testbed measuring force versus deflection perpendicularly at the tip of the assembled actuator under combined positive inflation and vacuum pressures.
Three-actuator robotic gripper grasping test setup lifting a hollow plastic carrier loaded incrementally with steel balls until grasp failure.

Detachable soft glove load capacity setup testing an empty glove (without a human hand) pressurized at 165 kPa and -85 kPa vacuum grasping a plastic bucket filled incrementally with water until failure.
Uniaxial tensile testing setup measuring silicone rubber stress-strain response and comparative peel/tensile tests evaluating Velcro adhesive methods.
future_work: Further research into 3D printing materials and advanced printing devices suitable for soft robotics.
Exploring application prospects of stiffness-tunable soft actuators in medical devices, biomimetic robots, and immersive haptic feedback for VR/AR.
Adding or replacing specialized sensing and driving units onto the modular soft gloves for diverse working tasks.
independent_variables: Vacuum pressure inside wire jamming envelope (e.g., 0 kPa, -30 kPa, -60 kPa, -85 kPa)
Jamming medium material (kraft rope, hemp rope, nylon wire, and kraft paper layer jamming for comparison)
Jamming structure thickness d (4 mm, 6 mm, 8 mm)
Deflection distance in bending tests (0 to 15 mm)
Rotation angle in torsion tests (0° to 60°)
Positive inflation air pressure Pin inside the fiber-reinforced actuator (0 to 165 kPa)
Wire arrangement geometry (circular vs. rectangular cross-section; trimmed vs. untrimmed free ends)
limitations_inferred: Vacuum pressurization and evacuation response times and dynamic switching bandwidth between jammed and unjammed states were not measured or reported.

Long-term durability, cyclic fatigue life, and wear characteristics of the inter-wire friction contact, Velcro fastener attachment, and thin 0.08 mm HDPE envelope under repeated bending cycles were not investigated.
The manual reverse-gradient trimming of wire ends is empirical and may pose repeatability or manufacturing challenges for automated production.

The Euler-Bernoulli beam model treats wires as either completely independent or fully monolithic, without capturing microscopic stick-slip contact mechanics, friction distribution, or 3D cross-sectional deformation.
Glove payload tests were performed without a human hand inside, leaving ergonomics, human-robot interaction forces, and biomechanical compliance unaddressed.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Assembly of the wire jamming structure significantly reduces the bending performance of the actuator, requiring higher positive air pressure (145 kPa vs. 87 kPa) to achieve a 90° bending angle.
Bending induces a gradient elongation effect at the free end of the wires, which can cause localized twisting, arching, and irreversible envelope deformation if untrimmed or unaccommodated.
Circular wire packing arrangements are prone to wire circumferential sliding during bending, resulting in misalignment and pre-jamming.
Nylon wire exhibits high initial unjammed stiffness and localized rearrangement, whereas hemp rope displays lower jammed stiffness due to thin surface fiber branches.
Layer jamming structures outperform wire jamming structures in bending stiffness and stiffness range, but wire jamming is inferior in single-plane bending stiffness.
Excessive jamming structure thickness increases initial unjammed stiffness, overall structure volume, and gradient elongation severity.
Velcro is inextensible, restricting its combination with stretchable substrate materials in wearable devices.
Current 3D printing technologies suffer from limitations in speed, material compatibility, and resolution when fabricating soft robotic components.
main_results: All three tested wire jamming media (kraft rope, hemp rope, nylon wire) exhibited substantial stiffness increases when transitioning from 0 kPa to -60 kPa vacuum pressure, with kraft rope selected for its balance of low initial unjammed stiffness and high jammed stiffness without rearrangement.
Adopting a rectangular wire arrangement and reverse-gradient trimmed wire ends successfully mitigated circumferential sliding, pre-jamming, and localized twisting/arching during bending.
For an 8 mm thick kraft rope jamming structure, switching vacuum from 0 to -85 kPa increased bending stiffness nearly seven-fold (achieving 0.89 N/mm at 15 mm deflection).

Wire jamming structures exhibited lower torsional impedance and smoother rotational response (0° to 60°) than layer jamming structures, with torsional stiffness increasing from 32.63 to 47.5 N*mm as thickness increased from 6 mm to 8 mm.
The assembled stiffness-tunable actuator achieved higher resistance to external tip deflections under -85 kPa vacuum across multiple bending states.
A soft robotic gripper equipped with three assembled actuators doubled its maximum payload grasping capacity when vacuum pressure was shifted from 0 to -85 kPa.
An unassisted detachable soft glove lifted a water bucket load exceeding 10,000 g under 165 kPa positive pressure and -85 kPa vacuum pressure.
modeling_methods: Euler-Bernoulli cantilever beam theoretical modeling for unjammed (individual independent beams) and jammed (unified solid composite beam) wire states.
Theoretical modeling of the fiber-reinforced soft actuator bending behavior to determine actuator geometric parameters.
Finite element (FE) simulation of the fiber-reinforced soft actuator bending state under positive air pressure.
performance_metrics: Bending stiffness (N/mm, defined as the ratio of applied force to deflection)
Bending stiffness increase ratio under vacuum (up to ~7x increase at -85 kPa vs. 0 kPa)
Torsional torque (N*mm) and torsional stiffness range (ratio between jammed and unjammed states, 1.88 to 2.02)
Free bending angle (degrees) as a function of positive air pressure (kPa)
Maximum payload mass of the soft robotic gripper (g)
Maximum lifting weight capacity of the detachable soft glove (g / kg)
Initial (unjammed) stiffness and stiffness variation range
possible_gap_implications: The deliberate choice of wire jamming to maintain low torsional impedance facilitates multi-DOF dexterous compliance, but this lower torsional rigidity could be a drawback in applications requiring high resistance to out-of-plane torsional perturbations during heavy grasping.

The substantial increase in positive inflation pressure required to bend the actuator once the jamming layer is attached (145 kPa vs. 87 kPa for 90°) highlights an inherent trade-off between passive unjammed compliance and overall variable-stiffness payload capacity.
Relying on manual wire trimming and heat-sealed thin HDPE envelopes reveals an open engineering gap in automated, robust manufacturing methods for multidirectional fiber/wire jamming skins.
paper.research_objective: To design, model, and fabricate a stiffness-tunable soft actuator based on a wire/fiber jamming mechanism with wide-range stiffness variation, universal adaptability, and high dexterity, utilizing a modular Velcro attachment scheme for rapid detachment and integration into soft robotic grippers and wearable exoskeletons.
paper.research_problem: Soft actuators suffer from low stiffness and hyper-elastic properties that restrict their use in high-load, high-speed, and precision tasks; conventional stiffening approaches often reduce flexibility, particle jamming can cause passive pre-jamming that limits bending range, and layer jamming is primarily restricted to single-plane deformation. In addition, existing stiffness-tunable soft actuators frequently rely on permanent adhesion or non-modular integration, making component replacement difficult upon leakage or wear.
paper.robot_type: Fiber-reinforced soft pneumatic actuator, soft robotic gripper, and wearable exoskeleton (detachable soft glove and detachable elbow sleeve)
paper.title: Detachable Soft Actuators with Tunable Stiffness Based on Wire Jamming
